channel.title: SVG and CSS :: K-State CC 120 Textbook
channel.description: When using inline SVG, you can apply CSS to the SVG using any of the methods we’ve used with HTML - inline styles, the <style> element, or a CSS file. The rules work exactly the same - you select a SVG element using a CSS selector, and apply style rules. SVG elements have tag name, and can also specify id and class attributes just like HTML. For example: <style> rect { fill: purple; stroke: black; stroke-width: 5; } #my-circle { fill: violet; stroke: #333; } </style> <svg viewBox="0 0 300 100" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"> <rect x="10" y="10" width="80" height="80"/> <circle id="my-circle" cx="200" cy="50" r="40"/> </svg>
